text: Jacek Karpiński was born in 1927 in Turin, Italy, into a family of Polish intellectuals and alpinists. His father, Adam Karpiński, was a prominent aeronautic engineer and inventor, while his mother, Wanda Czarnocka-Karpińska, was a respected physician. During World War II, Karpiński joined the Gray Ranks, a Polish underground paramilitary organization, and participated in numerous operations, including the Warsaw Uprising. After the war, he moved to Radomsko and later to Warsaw, where he completed his high school education and earned a degree in physics. He worked at the Polish Academy of Sciences' Institute of Basic Problems, where he designed the AAH — Analytical Analyzer of Harmonics. In 1959, he co-developed AKAT-1, the world's first differential equations analyzer based on transistors, which was praised for its innovative design and aesthetic appeal. Karpiński also contributed to the development of the KAR-65 computer, a significant technological achievement in Poland. He later founded the Microcomputers' Construction Plant (Zakład Budowy Mikrokomputerów) in 1970, aiming to create a minicomputer with advanced features, although the project was limited by political and economic challenges. After facing difficulties in securing commercial success, Karpiński returned to rural life in Olsztyn and later moved to Switzerland, where he worked on Nagra tape recorders. In the 1990s, he served as an advisor on computer science to prominent figures. Karpiński was awarded the Officer's Cross of Polonia Restituta in 2009 and posthumously received the Commander's Cross of Polonia Restituta in 2010. He died in 2010 in Wrocław.
